This lecture uses experimental clinopyroxene (CPX) chemistry to study **linear regression** and temperature prediction. The exercises below use the same experimental dataset, frozen train/evaluation allocation and Python models as the slides.

## Today’s objectives {.unnumbered}

- Fit and interpret simple and multiple linear regression, least squares, coefficients, p-values and $R^2$.
- Examine residual diagnostics, polynomial terms and interactions.
- Understand overfitting, training/test separation, model-search complexity, AIC and grouped cross-validation.
- Interpret prediction errors, confidence intervals for a conditional mean and prediction intervals for an individual observation.
- Distinguish association from causation and discuss scientific limitations.

## Exercises

Each exercise mixes short multiple-choice questions (with feedback) and editable Python cells. Select the **Hints** or **Solution** tab when you need help. The Python cells run in the browser, with an internet connection required to load the runtime and its packages.

**Core practice (start here; about 55–70 minutes):**

1. [Fit and understand a regression line](class_4_ex_1.qmd) — plot experimental CPX and interpret the MgO slope and $R^2$.
2. [Multiple regression with three oxides](class_4_ex_2.qmd) — fit models with MgO, Al₂O₃ and TiO₂; distinguish conditional coefficients.
3. [Residuals and curved relationships](class_4_ex_3.qmd) — inspect a diagnostic plot and fit the full quadratic.
4. [Test-set prediction error](class_4_ex_4.qmd) — respect publication groups and calculate RMSE and MAE.

**Extensions (if time permits; about 25–35 minutes):**

5. [AIC and grouped cross-validation](class_4_ex_5.qmd) — compare fixed candidates without using the evaluation partition for selection.
6. [Prediction intervals and scientific use](class_4_ex_6.qmd) — compare uncertainty for a mean and an individual experimental temperature.

The results describe **experimental** CPX in this teaching dataset. They do not, by themselves, validate temperature prediction for natural crystals. The evaluation results shown in the lecture have already been inspected; they should not be presented as a fresh blind test.
